steps.title: Two sketches to start
steps.text: I sketched both views first. The Story: a title, notes and a canvas, five steps max. The map: the output in the middle, everything else around it.

steps.title: Context, not a grid
steps.text: Newron opened on a gallery, an Are.na-style grid where every block weighs the same and none says why it's there. I wanted each reference kept with its reason, and the big things bigger, so the grid became a map around the result.

wipe.alt: The same collection as a grid of equal blocks, wiping into a map where each picture sits around the result with its reason beside it

said.text: references should have context, and information should not have the same hierarchy

steps.title: Told like a story
steps.text: Bullet points read like an article. I asked for it told like a story, warm and conversational, in the voice of whoever did the work.

said.text: the tone should be very conversational and reflects the tone of the user.

steps.title: Six strong calls, not a replay
steps.text: My first map just replayed the story: the same steps, the same pictures, even the same dates. I cut it to six strong calls, some heavier, each holding what the story doesn't.

wipe.alt: The first map showed the same three steps, with the same pictures and dates, then wipes into the weighted map with a large quote and the ticket

said.text: it should not be a replicate of the story.

steps.title: My notes became the rules
steps.text: I asked whether these fixes lived anywhere but this mockup. They didn't, so each of my notes became a rule in the backend's prompt. Every session's Story and Map now follows them.

rows.rule: At most five steps, in order. Each step is one major turn …

note.text: why does every node look very balanced?

rows.rule: The gallery sizes nodes by weight, so not everything can be major.

note.text: the entire reading experience should be like story-telling.

rows.rule: text: one paragraph of 15–45 words, written in the first person as the human, in their voice.
